summary: Read a positive integer n. It is the number of stairs between the ground and the top. Each move may cover one stair or two stairs, and either choice may be used again on later moves. Different orders of those choices count as different methods. Count the methods that start on the ground and reach the top, and write that count. Moving downward is forbidden, and a single move may not cover three stairs or more. The integer n is at least 1. Write only the count, not a list of the moves.
notes: Compare after trimming trailing newlines. The input is tokens in the same order as the method parameters.
